Since 1989, SHI International Corp. has helped organizations change the world through technology. We’ve grown every year since, and today we’re proud to be a $16 billion global provider of IT solutions and services.

Over 17,000 Organizations Worldwide Rely On SHI’s Concierge Approach To Help Them Solve What’s Next. But The Heartbeat Of SHI Is Our Employees – All 7,000 Of Them. If You Join Our Team, You’ll Enjoy

Our commitment to diversity, as the largest minority- and woman-owned enterprise in the U.S.
Continuous professional growth and leadership opportunities.
Health, wellness, and financial benefits to offer peace of mind to you and your family.
World-class facilities and the technology you need to thrive – in our offices or yours.

Job Summary

The Data Analyst collaborates with SHI management to support data-driven requests and initiatives, conducting data collection, analysis, and performance tracking across various segments. This role involves generating and merging reports from multiple databases, writing PowerBI reports, and performing ad-hoc analysis to identify opportunities and develop scenarios. The Data Analyst will assist with business cases, deliver monthly and quarterly reporting on financial and operational KPIs, and work closely with stakeholders to enhance data for analysis and performance management.

Role Description

Collaborate with SHI management to support numerous requests and project initiatives including from other SHI departments based on data.
Data collection & analysis of activity including forecasts across various segments and milestones.
Track & detail activity and performance against goals, forecasts and Plan.
Account Mapping by locating the appropriate salesperson for assigned list of leads.
Generate reports from multiple databases/data sets merging into spreadsheets and/or database.
Write reports in PowerBI for reporting and performance management.
Analyze, interpret, format, and summarize data for management review.
Work with stakeholders to obtain, validate, and enhance data utilized for analysis and performance tracking.
Perform ad-hoc analysis that aids in identifying opportunities, creating assumptions, and developing scenarios.
Assist with business cases defined with clear scope, intended outcomes, quantifiable benefits, and expenses.
Monthly and quarterly reporting focused on the entire portfolio of initiatives. This will include:
Financial performance: measure expense and savings on a profit and loss statement (P&L), cash flow impact, working capital impact, or productivity benefit.

Operational KPIs: tracking hours saved, utilization, # of instances, etc., depending on the project.

Commentary: work with initiative owners to identify drivers for the month, quarter, and future outcomes.

Behaviors and Competencies

Analytical Thinking: Can apply critical thinking to analyze data, identify patterns, and make basic inferences.
Data Analysis: Can identify patterns and trends in data, propose hypotheses, and use statistical techniques to test them.
Data Literacy: Can identify relevant data sources, collect data, and use basic tools to interpret and report findings.
Critical Thinking: Can analyze and interpret data to inform decision-making, and propose solutions based on logical reasoning.
Attention to Detail: Can identify errors or inconsistencies in work and make necessary corrections.
Communication: Can effectively communicate complex ideas and information, and can adapt communication style to the audience.
Problem-Solving: Can identify problems, propose solutions, and take action to resolve them without explicit instructions.
Technical Expertise: Can apply technical knowledge and skills effectively in most situations, with occasional guidance.
Time Management: Can generally use time effectively and is working towards improving task prioritization and deadline management.
Continuous Improvement: Can identify moderate areas for improvement and implement moderate changes.

Skill Level Requirements

Database management and reporting skills - Intermediate
Strong organizational skills - Intermediate
Experience with customer relations and satisfaction - Intermediate
Ability to multitask and complete tasks with efficiency and accuracy - Intermediate
Ability to follow direction while working individually and in a team environment - Intermediate
Ability to accept, understand, and learn from management feedback - Intermediate
Ability to work effectively within all levels of an organization, both internally and externally - Intermediate
Strong negotiation skills with the ability to influence stakeholders - Intermediate

Other Requirements

Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience required.
2-4 years of experience in a data and analysis-related field.
Advanced knowledge of Microsoft Excel & Access for reporting and database management
Proficient with Microsoft Office applications
Working knowledge of finance concepts, principles, and practices preferred.

jobs.title: Assoc/AVP, Business Analyst, Technology Group
jobs.description:
GIC is one of the world’s largest sovereign wealth funds. With over 2,000 employees across 11 locations around the world, we invest in more than 40 countries globally across asset classes and businesses. Working at GIC gives you exposure to an extraordinary network of the world’s industry leaders. As a leading global long-term investor, we Work at the Point of Impact for Singapore’s financial future, and the communities we invest in worldwide.

Enterprise and Data Technology

Enterprise & Data Technology builds and advances the technology that underpins our enterprise and data capabilities. It brings together our core technology and data experts to design and deliver platforms for integration, analytics, and innovation. By combining these strengths into one coordinated group, we create seamless solutions that connect systems, improve data accessibility, and leverage AI at the platform level to enable smarter decision-making. Through modern, scalable, and secure technology, the team empowers the organisation with tools that drive insight, collaboration, and operational excellence.

Enterprise Data & Analytics (EDA)

Enterprise Data & Analytics (EDA) harnesses one of GIC’s most valuable assets — data — to generate insights, drive outcomes and solve complex business challenges. We ingest, analyse and contextualise data across industries and asset classes to support investment decision-making and enhance investment processes. Together, we are building a high-performance enterprise data infrastructure, developing outcome-oriented data products and enabling GIC’s transformation into a data-driven organisation.

What will you do in this role?

As a risk-focused business analyst, you will partner with GIC’s top-of-the-house investment and risk professionals, shaping transformational capabilities that power critical investment data and analytics. You will collaborate across teams to build out impactful solutions and build new risk capabilities with significant room to grow as the capability scales out. This role supports GIC’s vision of being a data- and technology-driven global long-term investment firm.

Be part of an ambitious technology team supporting top-of-the-house investment activities, where data and analytics capabilities directly influence the long-term risk and reward profile of GIC’s total portfolio.

Play a pivotal role in the design, build and adoption of technology solutions consumed by investment and risk professionals across the firm, working closely with solution architects and subject matter experts to build robust, scalable and impactful data products.
Engage senior business stakeholders, data management teams and technology partners to align priorities, manage trade-offs and drive tangible, high-impact business outcomes.
Develop domain understanding of investment risk processes and technology capabilities, and apply this knowledge to shape data strategy, solution design and delivery execution.
Communicate and translate complex investment and risk questions into implementable requirements, contributing to model design, implementation, validation.
Manage the delivery of business solutions by applying strong analytical judgement, shaping delivery requirements, and priorities, as well as guiding teams to create measurable data and technology value for the business.
Proactively share learnings and provide guidance to team members to uplift service levels and deepen business knowledge across the team.
Streamline processes effectively to leverage on platforms, technology and artificial intelligence (AI) tools, applying AI to accelerate workstreams while continuously assessing improvements and innovations.

What impact can you make in this role?

You will lead strategic outcomes for GIC’s top-of-the-house investment and risk professionals, shaping transformational capabilities that power critical investment data and analytics. This role supports GIC’s vision of being a data- and technology-driven global long-term investment firm.

What makes you a successful candidate?

Join us if you are passionate about data and technology, and are motivated to lead the development of GIC’s enterprise data foundation, infrastructure and analytics capabilities.

4-8 years of relevant data and technology experience, preferably in financial services, risk or asset management, including collaborating with cross-functional business analysis, data and engineering teams to deliver impactful outcomes.
Good experience in the following:
Developing structured plans for the execution of data and technology solutions to uplift processes in relation to business analytics.
Defining business and functional specifications, and operationalizing it to unlock business value
Engaging senior stakeholders to influence adoption of data solutions
Working with SQL and Python, relational database queries, and modern data platforms such as Databricks and Snowflake

Type: Full-time

About Avari

 Avari is a fast-growing short-term rental property management company, operating in partnership with Casago across Florida's Gulf Coast, Alabama, Utah, Nevada, Oregon, and the Lake Tahoe region of California. As we continue to expand through strategic acquisitions and new market growth, we help homeowners maximize the value of their vacation rental investments through exceptional management and proven returns. This role plays a key part in strengthening our market expansion, sales outreach, and revenue operations as we scale nationwide.

About the role

As a Sales Operations Associate with Avari Management, this role sits at the intersection of data and the field. You'll mine market-level data to surface homeowner-acquisition opportunities in our priority markets, translate those insights into clear messaging and collateral for our reps, and provide the sales operations backbone — quota tracking, payouts, and forecasting support — that keeps the team running.

In short: you turn "here's what the data says" into "here's exactly what our reps should say and send," and you keep the numbers behind the sales team honest and current. You're happiest with a lot of surface area, moving fast, and a mix of analysis, communication, and operations in a single week.v

What you'll do

Market intelligence & analysis

Mine internal and third-party data (CRM, data warehouse, STR market data, property/ownership records) to identify high-opportunity markets, owner segments, and competitive dynamics.

Build repeatable market profiles covering owner density, competitor presence, pricing, seasonality, and regulatory considerations.

Partner with RevOps on enrichment workflows so the data feeding the field stays accurate and current.

Messaging & collateral

Translate market insights into clear value propositions tailored by market and owner segment.

Create rep-ready collateral: one-pagers, outreach/email templates, call scripts, market briefs, and objection-handling guides.

Keep the content library organized so reps can find and use what they need.

Sales enablement & adoption

Equip BD/sales reps with the market playbooks, messaging, and collateral they need to win owners in each region.

Onboard and train reps on positioning, tooling, and plays, and drive real adoption — not just published assets.

Run feedback loops with reps to learn what's landing in-market and refine accordingly.

Sales operations support

Track quota attainment across the sales team and calculate commission/payouts accurately and on time.

Support forecasting and pipeline reporting, including operating the team's pipeline-weighting and projected-revenue reporting.

Maintain CRM hygiene and build reporting that connects rep activity and enablement to pipeline and owner signings.

What you'll bring

Required

3–4 years in sales/revenue operations, sales enablement, analytics, growth, or another data-forward GTM role.

Strong with data
— you pull, analyze, and interpret it without hand-holding. Fluent in spreadsheets and CRM, and quick to pick up SQL or BI tools.

Tech-native
— you learn new tools fast and instinctively look for ways to automate and streamline.

Communicate insights well
— you turn a dataset into a clear, persuasive narrative and into material a rep can actually use.

High energy and pace
— you thrive with lots of moving parts, ambiguity, and a fast tempo, and you take ownership without waiting to be told.

Comfort with numbers behind a sales team: quota, commissions/payouts, and forecasting mechanics (or a clear aptitude to ramp quickly).

Preferred

Experience in proptech, real estate, hospitality, marketplaces, franchise/multi-location, or other geographically segmented go-to-market models.

HubSpot and/or data-warehouse (e.g., Snowflake) experience.

Familiarity with prospecting/enrichment tooling (e.g., Clay) and STR or local-market data sources.

Exposure to owner-, SMB-, or B2B2C-acquisition motions.

What success looks like

First 90 days:

jobs.title: Senior Technical Business Analyst – Data
jobs.description:
Job Title

Senior Technical Business Analyst – Data

Job Description

This is a senior, high-impact Business Analysis role for someone who combines structured BA capability with strong technical understanding of enterprise data delivery. You will lead complex data requirements from discovery through delivery, produce clear specifications for data integrations and semantic models, and influence senior stakeholders on the right approach.

This is not a reporting, dashboard-development or pure Data Analyst position. The successful candidate will be a Business Analyst first, with the technical credibility to work effectively with Data Architecture and Engineering teams.

What You’ll Be Doing

Lead business analysis for data delivery:

Lead the initiation, discovery, requirements definition and delivery of data-focused initiatives across underwriting, operations and finance.
Apply a structured Business Analysis approach across the full software development lifecycle, maintaining traceability from business need through to delivered outcome.
Take ownership of complex workstreams and smaller data projects, providing direction to colleagues and reducing reliance on senior leaders for day-to-day stakeholder management.
Contribute to the evolution of BA standards, templates, quality controls and ways of working across the data function.

Specify Enterprise Data Solutions

Produce clear, engineering-ready specifications for data integrations, including source and target structures, mappings, transformation and business rules, validation, data-quality controls, dependencies, exception handling and acceptance criteria.
Define requirements for semantic models, data warehouse solutions and analytical data platforms, distinguishing between specifying a solution and building it directly.
Use data flows, lineage, source-to-target mappings, reporting specifications and conceptual or logical data models to remove ambiguity and support scalable delivery.
Work with Data Architecture and Engineering teams to clarify requirements, challenge assumptions and maintain shared understanding throughout delivery.

Influence Stakeholders And Shape Delivery

Lead workshops and conversations with senior business and technical stakeholders, including where priorities, viewpoints or levels of technical understanding differ.
Translate complex data concepts into concise, practical recommendations that enable stakeholders to understand and support the proposed approach.
Build commitment to delivery plans and technical direction, escalating only where appropriate.
Support adoption and transition into business as usual, ensuring the solution addresses the original business need.

Embed Governance And Data Quality

Embed data ownership, definitions, standards, controls and quality requirements into specifications and delivery.
Support data-quality assessment, issue definition, remediation requirements and agreement of measurable acceptance criteria.
Ensure delivery aligns with enterprise data strategy, governance expectations and the organisation’s regulated operating environment.

What Success Looks Like

Engineering teams receive sufficiently detailed, unambiguous specifications to design and build integrations and data products effectively.
Senior stakeholders understand the proposed approach, trade-offs and implications and are confident supporting the delivery plan.
Business needs remain traceable from discovery through requirements, build, validation and adoption.
The permanent team develops stronger technical BA capability, consistent standards and less dependency on contractors or senior leaders.
Data governance and quality are built into delivery rather than addressed after implementation.

Essential Experience

What we’re looking for

Proven experience as a Senior Business Analyst or Senior Technical Business Analyst delivering data-centric initiatives end to end.
Demonstrable experience producing specifications for enterprise data integrations, data warehouses or semantic models for delivery by Engineering teams.
Strong understanding of the software development lifecycle and how requirements move from discovery through build, testing, acceptance and adoption.

jobs.title: Senior Program Manager, AIR Opportunity Fund
jobs.description:
The AIR Opportunity Fund is seeking a Senior Program Officer
to support and advance the Fund’s grantmaking, research, and partnership activities focused on expanding opportunity and improving outcomes for communities across the United States. As the AIR Opportunity Fund builds depth in workforce and economic opportunity, health, and youth pathways, we are seeking candidates who can strengthen our presence in the Midwest, the Washington, DC, area, or the Deep South. The Senior Program Officer will bring subject-matter knowledge in one or more of these areas, familiarity with the communities and regions we serve, and the initiative to move work forward with direction from senior staff. Working closely with portfolio managers and directors, the Senior Program Officer will lead significant components of the Fund’s grantmaking and programmatic initiatives, provide strategic and analytical guidance, and cultivate relationships with grantees, community leaders, researchers, funders, and other key stakeholders. The ideal candidate will bring substantial experience spanning applied research and philanthropy, demonstrated leadership of complex initiatives and partnerships, and the ability to use evidence and field knowledge to inform strategy, funding decisions, and continuous learning. The Fund's strategic priorities and major grantmaking commitments are largely established, and this role will focus on stewarding existing grants and partnerships, monitoring progress, and supporting implementation and learning activities, rather than sourcing, developing, or approving new grants at this time. The selected candidate will work remotely but must be based in or near one of the Fund's priority regions: the Midwest (Chicago or Cleveland preferred), the greater Washington, DC, area, or the Delta Region (Arkansas, Alabama, or Mississippi preferred). Travel to AIR Opportunity Fund events is expected up to 30%. This position has the flexibility to work remotely within the United States (U.S.) or from one of AIR’s U.S. office locations. This does not include U.S. territories.

About AIR

Founded in 1946 and headquartered in Arlington, Virginia, the American Institutes for Research (AIR) is a nonpartisan, not-for-profit organization that conducts behavioral and social science research and delivers technical assistance to address some of the most pressing challenges in the United States and globally. We generate evidence and apply data-driven solutions that expand opportunities and improve lives for all.

Responsibilities

The responsibilities for the position include:

Manage assigned components of programmatic initiatives from planning through implementation and evaluation under the direction of portfolio managers and directors.
Represent the Fund at conferences, community meetings, and field-based events within the assigned region, and nationally, as needed.
Manage multiple projects and workstreams simultaneously, ensuring timely completion of deliverables.
Conduct research, landscape analyses, and environmental scans to inform funding decisions, program priorities, and new initiatives.
Synthesize research findings, field insights, and grantee learnings into reports, briefings, presentations for internal and external audiences.
Manage relationships with grantees, community organizations, researchers, and other stakeholders.
Coordinate meetings, convenings, site visits, and other stakeholder engagement activities.
Contribute subject-matter knowledge in workforce and economic opportunity, health, and/or youth pathways.
Review grant proposals, conduct due diligence, and develop funding recommendations.
Monitor grant and program performance, track outcomes, and identify opportunities for learning and improvement.
Collaborate with AIR researchers, subject matter experts, and operational staff.

Qualifications

Education, Knowledge, and Experience

Master's degree in public policy, public health, social sciences, education, nonprofit management, community development, or a related field.
Minimum of seven years of professional experience that includes both applied research and philanthropy, grantmaking, social impact investing, or related funding experience.
Subject matter expertise in one or more priority areas: workforce and economic opportunity, health, and/or youth pathways.
Demonstrated knowledge of the communities, organizations, and policy or funding landscape within communities and regions served by the Fund, particularly the Deep South, Cleveland, Chicago, and/or Washington, DC region.
Demonstrated experience using research, evaluation, or data-driven approaches to inform program design, funding decisions, strategy, or organizational learning.
Experience managing or supporting grant portfolios, philanthropic initiatives, research projects, or community-based programs.
Experience working with community-based organizations, research institutions, public agencies, philanthropic organizations, or cross-sector partnerships.
Demonstrated ability to manage multiple projects and priorities simultaneously while producing high-quality work.

Skills

Strong research, analytical, and critical thinking skills, with the ability to evaluate evidence and identify actionable insights.
Effective communication skills, including public speaking and presentation skills and the ability to translate complex information for a variety of audiences.
Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to build productive relationships across a variety of stakeholders.
Strong relationship-management and influencing skills, with the ability to establish credibility and build productive relationships with community leaders, grantees, researchers, funders, and other stakeholders.
Advanced project and program management skills, including experience leading complex initiatives involving multiple stakeholders, priorities, and deadlines.
Ability to work independently while contributing effectively within a collaborative team environment.
Willingness to travel nationally, as needed.

new_jobs.title: Technical Project Manager II
new_jobs.description:
About Torus

Torus is headquartered in Utah and is expanding manufacturing at our 545,000-square-foot facility in Salt Lake City called GigaOne. We are

the world’s first mesh energy infrastructure, uniting communities through resilient, sustainable, and intelligent power.

We design, engineer, manufacture, install, and support our systems end-to-end, standing behind them throughout their lifecycle. Torus systems help reduce costs, lower emissions, and protect facilities from outages, while strengthening the security and reliability of the broader utility grid. Torus is committed to American manufacturing, engineering excellence, and building energy systems that last.

Torus has raised over $267 million from investors like Magnetar, Mercado, ICONIQ and Origin Ventures. The investments are helping to accelerate deployment of modular power plants across utilities, data centers, and industrial sectors. This investor confidence reflects the strength of our team, technology as well as the scale of the problem we are solving.

At Torus, you will be part of something larger than a single product or technology. Your work will help build energy infrastructure that supports and strengthens our electrical grid, critical systems, industry, and communities for decades to come. We value accountability, collaboration, and clear thinking. We are looking for people who want to solve hard problems and build things that matter.

About The Role

The Technical Project Manager II

will own the schedule, scope, and coordination of Torus site builds, from design freeze through procurement, construction, commissioning, and handoff to operations. Our sites are built from repeatable units and scale to hundreds of nodes, so the work is as much about sequencing vendors, lead times, and dependencies as it is about any single task.

This is a hands-on role for someone who is technical enough to understand what a delayed optic, an unconfirmed carrier handoff, or an unbalanced PDU branch does to a go-live date, and is organized enough to keep many parallel workstreams moving. You will work daily with network, compute, and systems engineers, facilities and electrical contractors, carriers, and equipment vendors, and you will be the person who knows what is blocked, why, and what happens next.

Who You Are

You work comfortably between technical depth and cross-functional pace, whether you’re in a design review, a change-window call, or a vendor escalation.

You see the whole system. You know how a delayed optics shipment or a firmware hold ripples into site turn-up, security review, and handoff to operations, and you use data to plan around it.
You lead with the answer. You turn complex technical discussions into a clear answer, an owner, and a deadline. Your status updates, runbooks, and stand-ups keep people aligned without adding process.
You earn trust across teams. Network, compute, systems, security, and facilities engineers know you’ll ask about their constraints before asking them to move faster.
You hold speed and quality together. You push for urgency and still insist on testing, validation, and rollback plans before anything goes into production.
You let the customer break the tie. Your customers are the sites, operators, and internal teams who depend on your uptime. When trade-offs get hard, you make the call with them in mind and help the team do the same.
You stay steady in ambiguity. Fast scale-up means incomplete information. You define a path forward anyway, share progress and setbacks directly, and meet blockers and incidents with realism and confidence in the team.

Responsibilities

Program planning and delivery

Own the integrated plan for each site build: scope, milestones, dependencies, critical path, and go-live criteria
Break each site into repeatable workstreams (network core, compute, power, cooling, fiber and cabling, security, telemetry) and track them against the plan
Run weekly cross-functional status meetings, maintain a single source of truth for schedule and risks, and produce clear status reports for leadership
Identify schedule risks early, propose mitigations, and escalate decisions that need an owner
Maintain a repeatable build playbook so that each new Pod or System is faster than the last

Procurement and supply chain

Work with engineering and procurement to turn designs into bills of materials, review vendor quotes for completeness (optics, cabling, licenses, support), and track open quote gaps to closure
Track orders, lead times, shipments, and receiving across multiple vendors, and flag long-lead items (switches, firewalls, optics, power and cooling equipment) at the start of each build
Coordinate RMAs, substitutions, and re-quotes without losing the schedule
Maintain an accurate inventory and delivery status for each site, including what is owned, ordered, and still missing

Site, power, and facilities coordination

Coordinate electrical, mechanical, and cooling work with facilities teams and contractors, including power feeds, PDUs, cooling distribution, and rack and cabinet readiness
Schedule and run change windows, power-on events, and cutovers, with rollback plans and clear communication
Track site readiness gates before equipment ships and before nodes are powered on
Manage on-site logistics for installation crews and technicians, including access, safety requirements, and sequencing

Carriers, ISPs, and external vendors

Manage circuit orders and turn-up with carriers, including demarc and handoff details, optics, BGP and IP-space requests, and install dates
Track address-space and registry applications that have long lead times
Manage vendor and contractor statements of work, deliverables, and acceptance
Be the single point of contact for external parties on schedule and dependencies

Commissioning and handoff

Define and track commissioning and acceptance criteria with engineering for each site
Drive punch lists to closure and confirm that documentation, runbooks, labeling, and as-built records are delivered before handoff
Coordinate the handoff of nodes and sites to operations and to customers or hosting partners, including credential, access, and onboarding checklists

Risk, change, and communication

Maintain a risk and issue register for each site, ranked by impact on availability and schedule
Apply change control to scope, schedule, and design changes, and communicate downstream impacts to cost, schedule, and other sites
Track budget against plan for each build and flag variances early
Document lessons learned after each build and feed them back into the playbook

Required Experience

5+ years of project management work
3-5 years of experience managing technical projects in data center, network, infrastructure, or construction environments
Demonstrated experience delivering projects with multiple vendors, long-lead procurement, and fixed go-live dates
Working technical fluency in networking and compute fundamentals (switches, firewalls, servers, optics and cabling, power and cooling) sufficient to challenge estimates and understand dependencies
Experience building and maintaining project plans, risk registers, and status reporting using standard tools (for example, Jira, Smartsheet, MS Project, or similar)
Experience reviewing vendor quotes, bills of materials, and statements of work
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work with engineers, executives, and external vendors
Ability to prioritize across many concurrent workstreams and make clear decisions with incomplete information
Comfort with change control and checklist-driven procedures
Willingness to travel within Utah, with occasional travel to remote sites

Preferred Experience

Experience on GPU or high-density compute deployments, or data center build-outs
Familiarity with liquid cooling, high-density power distribution, or colocation and facility coordination
Experience managing carrier circuit turn-ups and ISP or IP-address requests
Familiarity with OT/ICS or energy infrastructure environments
Experience with infrastructure automation or a technical background in systems or network engineering
Experience with budget tracking and cost reporting on capital projects
Project management certification (PMP, PRINCE2, or similar)
Experience with Jira or similar tools, including building dashboards from live data

Additional Details

Background Check:

All candidates are subject to a background check.

Location:

This role is a hybrid remote position based in Salt Lake City. The Technical Project Manager will be expected to travel to Torus locations in Utah, with occasional travel to remote sites.

Compensation:

$140,000 - 175,000 (Note: We have the flexibility to hire at different levels, which may impact the corresponding pay range.)

Work Authorization:

Applicants must already have the legal authorization to work in the US without requiring any employer sponsorship.

Physical Requirements

Constantly operates a computer and other peripheral office equipment such as a printer or mouse.
Ability to communicate information so others can understand. Must be able to exchange accurate information in these situations.
Must report to work reliably and with the ability to use full and unimpaired skills and judgment to safely execute your job.
Proficiency in reading, writing, and speaking English required.
When on the production floor, ability to observe, detect and respond to audible and visual machine malfunction warnings.
Ability to traverse uneven terrain during site surveys at construction and industrial sites, at times for extended periods.
Ability to ascend stairs and ladders and navigate active construction areas.
Ability to wear required PPE at job sites and on the production floor, such as a hard hat/safety helmet, safety glasses, ear protection, high-visibility apparel, and protective footwear.
Ability to lift up to 25 lbs occasionally.
Ability to work outdoors in varying weather.
Ability to work outside normal business hours for power-on events and cutovers.
Ability to travel to Torus sites in Utah and occasionally to remote sites.

Our Perks & Benefits

401(k) Retirement Savings Plan

Plan participants have access to telehealth services, mental health support and coaching, and exclusive discounts on brands, dining, entertainment, and more.

Time Off

10 paid company holidays
Waiting period-free 100% paid parental leave

Culture & Community

Regular company-wide offsites to showcase our progress and learnings. A time to step back, think strategically, and work on the business together.
Team members receive Torus branded gear
Peer Recognition Program
Fully stocked break rooms with free snacks and drinks. Because great work deserves great fuel.

About Vitae Health Systems:

Founded in 2018, Vitae Health Systems is one of the largest providers of behavioral health, internal medicine, and podiatry services to residents of Skilled Nursing and Assisted Living Facilities. Headquartered in Chicago, IL, we currently operate in over 10 states and are rapidly expanding throughout the USA.

Overview

Vitae launches its ACO under the CMS Long-term Enhanced ACO Design (LEAD) Model on January 1, 2027, building on our experience in ACO REACH High Needs. The VBC Program Manager builds and runs the operating rhythm of the LEAD ACO, making sure the work that drives results (beneficiary alignment, utilization, quality performance, and program compliance) is tracked, scheduled, and followed through on time.

This is a hands-on operating role. You will lead the VBC operations team, run the weekly and monthly performance cadence with the VBC data resource, and work with the VBC clinical team and operations managers to turn performance data into clear, prioritized actions. You own the calendar, the cadence, and the follow-through. Clinical standards and compliance decisions remain with clinical and compliance leadership.

Key Responsibilities

LEAD ACO Operating Cadence and Performance Tracking

Run the weekly team huddle and monthly performance review covering alignment, utilization, quality, and reported spend, using KPIs and targets set by VBC leadership
Track performance against the LEAD quality measures and Prevention and Quality Plan milestones, and report variances to leadership
Monitor utilization drivers (admissions, readmissions, ED visits, post-acute stays) and confirm high-risk patients have a named owner and documented action, escalating gaps to clinical leadership
Review operational CMS reports and data feeds monthly, flag variances early, and escalate risks with a recommended path
Maintain the master calendar of CMS deadlines and deliverables, with a named owner for each, and follow up so nothing is missed

Alignment and Compliance Oversight

Oversee the voluntary alignment program against leadership-set targets and deadlines, including a documented pre-submission review before each CMS submission
Oversee reconciliation of CMS alignment lists to census and EHR data, and lead root cause reviews on avoidable attrition (deaths, hospice elections, moves, Medicare Advantage enrollment)
Reconcile Participant and Preferred Provider lists to HR and credentialing records at the TIN/NPI level, escalating any change that needs a leadership or Compliance decision
Verify that beneficiary notifications and outreach activities are completed, tracked, and documented to CMS requirements, in partnership with Compliance

Cross-Functional Partnership

Work with operations managers on how VBC activities are scheduled and delivered at the facility and NP level, surfacing barriers early and avoiding unnecessary burden
Partner with VBC clinical leadership so workflows, checklists, and handoffs reflect clinical standards
Support development of provider-facing materials (scorecards, tip sheets, trainings) with the clinical and data owners, coordinating timelines and operational input

Data, Reporting & Continuous Improvement

Submit and sequence reporting requests to the VBC data resource through a single intake, review data for reasonableness before use in reviews, and flag manual work that could be automated
Prepare the performance summaries the Director of VBC Operations presents to senior leadership and ACO governance, aggregating data, clinical, and operational input
Lead root cause reviews when measures move off target and turn findings into action plans with named owners and due dates, tracking each to closure and routing clinical actions to clinical leadership
Facilitate a quarterly improvement cycle (plan, do, study, act) based on financial and performance results, with the Director of VBC Operations as sponsor: convene Finance, clinical, and data partners to select opportunities, assign actions, evaluate results, and document learning in a VBC operating playbook

Team Leadership

Lead the VBC operations team and serve as its first point of contact: coach, set priorities and escalation thresholds, build SOPs with process owners, and resolve operational questions and blockers within defined boundaries, escalating strategic, financial, compliance, and policy matters to the Director of VBC Operations
Provide input to the Director of VBC Operations on structure and staffing as scope grows

What Success Looks Like

First 90 days: The master CMS calendar is in place with named owners. The weekly and monthly cadence is running and escalation thresholds are defined. The first quarterly improvement cycle is launched, with opportunities, owners, measures, and evaluation dates set. Team members have clear goals and documented workflows
First year: Two or more improvement cycles are completed with documented results and feed a VBC operating playbook. Alignment, quality, and utilization are tracked against targets all year, with action plans when a measure is off target. Escalations arrive with context and a recommended path

Requirements

Required

Bachelor's degree in healthcare administration, public health, business, nursing, or a related field
4+ years in value-based care, ACO operations, or population health (provider-side strongly preferred)
Direct experience in a CMS ACO model (ACO REACH, especially High Needs, MSSP, or LEAD)
Experience in post-acute, SNF, or long-term care
2+ years managing staff
Track record running recurring operating cadences and hitting deadlines
Experience running structured improvement cycles (e.g., PDSA, Lean) and building playbooks
Working knowledge of CMS alignment (claims-based and voluntary), ACO quality measures, beneficiary protections and marketing requirements, and benchmark and settlement basics
Ability to drive follow-through across clinical, operational, and data teams without direct authority
Clear communicator who can explain data to clinicians and leaders, and is comfortable with financial and utilization reports, Excel, BI dashboards, and EHR data

Master's degree

new_jobs.description:
About YPO

YPO is a global leadership community of over 35,000 chief executives from more than 140 countries. YPO brings together extraordinary leaders who are committed to becoming better leaders and better people. The organization provides a platform for the leaders to connect, learn, and grow through shared experiences, rich learning programs, and meaningful relationships. Members benefit from a supportive community that fosters personal, business, family and community growth.

Supporting these members is a world-class management team of more than 450 associates, spanning over 25 countries. Our organization is based in Dallas, Texas, with many associates working virtually and outside of the United States. Together, our team of global associates works to create a truly Only-in-YPO experience for our members

Position Details

This is a remote work-from-home position.

Work Hours:
Candidates must be flexible to accommodate time zones of international stakeholders when necessary.

POSITION PURPOSE

The Leadership Services Program Manager (LSPM) partners with the Committee/Council Leads, Committee Chairs and Committee Members to support committee strategy planning and yearly activities, including delivery of information, content, and follow-up of their meetings/activities, work groups or special projects as required. Responsible for the implementation of planning process for the efficient execution of the yearly committee cycle. The program manager partners with the leadership community, coordinating logistics, governance, and operational alignment while promoting collaboration in support of the Board and Organization’s priorities. This will involve timely, professional, and high-touch communications with board members, member champions, internal, and external stakeholders/resources.

PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES

Manages the annual committee lifecycle, including planning, meeting preparation, milestones, decision documentation, action tracking and accountability for timely follow-through.
Manages all components of virtual and in-person committee and council meetings, including but not limited to scheduling, drafting content for agendas, facilitating, documenting key actions and decisions, and follow-up.
Builds trusted relationships with the Committee/Council Leads, Committee Chairs and Committee members to support committee strategy planning and yearly activities, optimizing idea sharing and best practices.
Facilitates the global and role-specific onboarding process for committee/council members, including training on YPO processes and systems to support their champion experience.
Ensures flawless execution of committee activities on site at the in-person bi-annual leadership meetings, including formal meetings, dinners, and additional experiences.
Develops and refines meeting agendas, pre-reading materials, meeting summaries and committee member communications.
Delivers consistent, accurate and up-to-date committee documents, including directories, calendars, reference materials, communication channels, data, templates, archives, et al.
Manages timely communication of announcements, discussions, and materials to member champions.
Supports elections processes and executes selection committee meetings for Board committees, Councils, and other roles when necessary.
Reviews and updates committee/council information on internal and external platforms as needed and at year-end ensuring committees are up to date and members are identified properly.
Fosters compliance and perpetuates alignment to all facets of YPO’s published Policies & Procedures, Code of Conduct, Core Principles, overall values, and applicable by-laws.
Ensures professional quality standards by developing and improving processes to support the fulfillment of goals and strategic implementation.
Recommends, develops, and socializes governance protocols for other management portfolios. Identifies trends, collaborations, and other opportunities related to governance.
Serves as the general point of contact for champion inquiries from members and management team.

SKILLS

Outstanding Business acumen, professionalism, and emotional intelligence to communicate effectively in a multi-cultural, virtual work environment with high-profile corporate leaders.
Excellent interpersonal skills, adept at building meaningful relationships with all levels of associates, members, and vendors. Adaptable, insightful, empathetic, and reliable. Great sense of humor and humility.
Able to maintain discretion and integrity of confidential information.
Resourceful and able to work independently with initiative and good judgement. Superior time management, planning, organization, and effective prioritization skills with the ability to focus on and navigate multiple projects simultaneously.
Possesses a distinct global mindset, sensitive to local and international customs and protocols.
Able to identify problems, research alternatives, provide solutions and/or resolve issues in a timely manner. Anticipates member needs and delivers with clarity.
Analytical thinker with ability influence and guide processes with appropriate approach and execution. Natural curiosity and desire to learn more; proficiency and interest in applying new technologies and tools.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills, including proof reading, with a meticulous attention to detail. Adjusts communication and working style appropriately for the global audience.
Professional presence, appearance, and stature to interact easily with YPO members, C-level executives, and high-profile corporate leaders.

EXPERIENCE/BACKGROUND

Minimum 5 years’ experience in professional services and/or event planning environments with multiple senior-level stakeholder groups globally.
Proven customer service experience in a high-touch environment where responsible for identifying and implementing alternative solutions and resolving issues in a timely manner.
Experience handling challenging situations with grace and tact, navigating, and simplifying with a positive attitude.
Proven experience in supporting, stewarding, and executing multiple stakeholder goals and deliverables successfully.
Membership or association experience preferred, with an understanding of governance structures, committees and consensus management.
Proven administrative skills. Prefer corporate executive level of administrative experience.
Experience working in a virtual work environment preferred.

EDUCATION/TRAINING/CERTIFICATION

Relevant bachelors university degree or equivalent experience required.
Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite and database management systems, preferably CRM.
PMP or CMP certifications preferred.
Proficient with virtual video conferencing platforms such as Zoom.
Must be fluent in English, written and verbal. Partial fluency or knowledge in other languages preferred.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

Ability to work flexible and/or extended hours as needed to accommodate members and team members in multiple time zones.
Ability to work for extended hours at a computer screen.
Willingness and ability to travel, domestically and internationally, without restrictions, approximately 5-7 times per year.

Compensation at YPO is one part of a broader Total Rewards philosophy built to attract, motivate, and retain talented people in every country and function where we operate. We aim to be fair, consistent, and thoughtful stewards of our resources, and we ground pay decisions in market data, role scope, and internal equity rather than negotiation alone.

Compensation ranges are based on the associate's primary work location. Because this role may be filled in more than one country, the applicable ranges are listed below by location:
For US applicants: USD 76,600–97,700 annually
For Canada applicants: CAD 76,500–97,500 annually
For Portugal applicants: EUR 36,400–45,500 annually

We believe pay is only part of how YPO invests in its people. Associates are also eligible for performance-based bonus opportunities, remote work flexibility, and a comprehensive rewards package built around their wellbeing and growth. Your Talent Acquisition Business Partner will share the details specific to your location as part of the interview process.

EOE

YPO does not discriminate in recruiting, hiring, training, promotion, or other employment practices for reasons of race, color, religion, gender, national origin, age, sexual orientation, marital or veteran status, disability, or any other legally protected status.

Work / Life Balance: 36 hour week, flexible working around core hours and Friday afternoons off, flexible working

Elevate your career at Airbus Belfast as our Business Operations Manager.
You will be the lead designer of our growth strategy, building a robust value stream through lean methodology and data-driven financial management. By bridging the gap between shop-floor operations and corporate support, you will ensure our facility remains a global benchmark for rate-readiness. We are looking for an influential leader to de-risk our supply chain and accelerate commercial success in a world-class aerospace hub.

This role is L2

How You Will Contribute To The Team

Strategic Integration & Risk Mitigation: You are the bridge between operations and support functions. You use the ARM (Active Risk Management) tool and TIP (Tactical Implementation Plans) to identify financial and operational bottlenecks, ensuring change management plans are executed to eradicate "hard-hitting" business problems.
Operational SQCDP Performance: You hold accountability for the Business Management System. By monitoring trends in Safety, Quality, Cost, Delivery, and People (SQCDP), you drive rate-readiness planning to ensure the airframe value stream can meet future build demands and increased production rates.
Financial & Resource Stewardship: You manage significant growth by exercising delegated budget authority over CAPEX, NRC (Non-Recurring Costs), NPO, and Indirect Payroll. You ensure the business is "resourced for the future" by aligning recruitment and training with long-term Airbus profitability goals

About You

Essential Technical & Operational Skills

Project Delivery & Management: Proven track record in delivering/implementing projects and managing operational performance.

Continuous Improvement:
Experience operating business management systems across SQCDP (Safety, Cost, Quality, Delivery, People) areas.

Financial Planning & Budget Management:
Financial planning skills for growth; ability to manage budget authority (NPO, NRC, CAPEX, Indirect Payroll).

Communication:
Ability to listen, adapt style to various audiences, share information openly, and resolve conflict.

Leadership & Influence:
Ability to inspire, motivate, and influence teams/stakeholders outside direct span of control.

Customer Focus:
Strategy development focused on adding value and exceeding customer expectations.

Results Orientation:
Driving performance through stretched, competitive targets

Desirable Skills

Leadership Experience:
Time spent within the organization as a leader.

Cross-Functional Integration: Demonstrated experience resolving issues across Engineering, Supply Chain, and support functions.

Risk & Tactical Planning:
Hands-on experience with risk mitigation tools (e.g., ARM) and formulation of Tactical Implementation Plans (TIP).

Workforce & Rate Readiness
Planning: Ability to conduct rate readiness planning to meet future build demands, along with recruiting and developing personnel.

Closing date: Thursday 26th November 2026

This role requires a level of spoken and/or written English that is necessary to carry out the duties of the position effectively. Equivalent qualifications or demonstrable experience will be considered.

Senior Implementation Manager - Teacher Education

Clinical Education SaaS | Remote (US) | $100,000 - $120,000 Base

About the Opportunity

We’re building a brand-new Teacher Education vertical for a category-leading clinical education SaaS company, and this role is the one that builds it. Rather than inheriting an existing book of business, you’ll stand up the entire implementation playbook for Teacher Education programs from the ground up - onboarding, configuration, accreditation and certification workflows, and field placement support - before moving into an ongoing account-ownership role once that foundation is proven.

What You’ll Do

Lead onboarding and implementation for new Teacher Education program clients, coordinating closely with Operations, Configuration, and Support to get programs live and running smoothly.
Build deep working knowledge of the platform so you can configure it to match how a Teacher Education program actually operates - field placement tracking, student teaching documentation, candidate progress monitoring.
Own the certification and accreditation side of implementation: understand CAEP standards and state certification requirements, and help programs configure the system to support their own compliance and reporting needs.
Act as the primary point of contact for new clients through their first year - troubleshooting issues, training staff, and embedding the platform into daily program operations.
Represent the business at Teacher Education conferences and build relationships with program leaders and prospective partners.
Partner with Sales on prospective accounts and with Product on roadmap feedback.
Once the playbook is established, transition into an ongoing Account Manager role, owning the long-term relationship for the programs you’ve implemented.

What We’re Looking For

We’re open to two different paths into this role, and genuinely value either:
Direct, hands-on experience with a Teacher Education or educator preparation program - as a Director of Teacher Education, Program Coordinator, Field Experience/Clinical Placement Coordinator, or similar, or

A proven account management, implementation, or sales background specifically within Teacher Education, educator preparation, or the broader K-12/higher-ed EdTech space, with genuine, demonstrated familiarity with how these programs operate and what they struggle with.

Either way, you should bring real familiarity with CAEP accreditation, state certification requirements, or student teaching/field placement workflows - this isn’t a role for someone learning the space from scratch, whether you’re coming from the program side or the vendor side. Strong cross-functional coordination instincts and comfort with technology adoption and training also matter, since you’ll be working across Operations, Configuration, Support, Sales, and Product from day one.

Why This Role

A genuine ground-floor build - you shape how this vertical works rather than inherit someone else’s process.
Deep domain credibility and proven commercial experience are both valued here - this role doesn’t require choosing one over the other.
A clear path from implementation into an ongoing account-ownership role.
Backed by a profitable, established business investing specifically in this growth vertical.

new_jobs.description:
Want to make a positive difference to the future of people and our one shared home, the Earth? Working at WWF could be your opportunity of a lifetime.

All around the world, people are waking up to the devastating impacts of climate change and nature loss. The situation today is worse than the darkest predictions of just ten years ago, pushing billions of people to the edge and threatening lives and livelihoods. At WWF, we are facing our biggest crisis – and our biggest ever opportunity – to create a better future for people and nature. With over 60 years of experience and an active presence in more than 100 countries, we work to achieve both on-the-ground and global policy action, from protecting and restoring species and their habitats, to transforming markets and policies toward sustainability.

Our people come from hugely diverse backgrounds and with a variety of expertise, ranging from conservation science and advocacy to HR and finance. We welcome applications from anyone who believes they can help us tackle this enormous global challenge and drive the urgent conservation impact needed to restore our planet.

What We Do

We are an independent conservation organization, striving to sustain the natural world for the benefit of people and the ecosystem. From individuals and communities to businesses and governments, we are part of a growing global movement calling for bolder action on climate and nature, demanding that world leaders set nature on the path to recovery by 2030. WWF works to address the most dominant drivers of nature loss through system-wide changes in how food and energy are produced and consumed, and in how financial systems are structured. By implementing change in every country, we aim to drive visible and positive impacts on the ground, helping to restore nature in the most critical places around the world, from the Amazon to the Coral Triangle.

Engaging everyone means addressing the barriers to participation faced by some groups in society, including local communities. Conservation will only be sustainable if it is owned by, and benefits, local people. That’s why Indigenous Peoples and local communities must be at the centre of action on climate and nature. WWF is committed to using its resources and global network to support these communities in creating together the most effective solutions where they live.

Humanity is still in time, we have a clear pathway to solve this crisis. At WWF, we call on everyone to join the global movement, change how we live, and take action now.

WWF International global recruitment team are exclusively managing this vacancy. We kindly ask that you do not contact the local office on this position.

As Senior Project Manager – Hazina Implementation, you hold day-to-day delivery accountability for Project Hazina, a strategic initiative to implement a unified, cloud-based Global Finance & Accounting System (GFAS) on Microsoft Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations. The goal of the project is to replace an ageing, fragmented finance systems landscape across more than 30 entities, including the Secretariat and its managed Country Offices. The project will be delivered over approximately two years.

You are accountable for delivering the project within the scope, schedule, budget and quality set by the project governance.

MISSION OF THE DEPARTMENT

To align and harmonise technology, digital and data capabilities across the WWF Network to enable conservation impact at scale while safeguarding the organisation and the people we work with, through fit for purpose solutions that are device and hardware agnostic, mobile functional, built on integrated, secure and scalable cloud enabled technology platforms and are consistently delivered and supported anytime anywhere.

Major Functions

Own end-to-end delivery of the Hazina implementation: build and maintain the master plan covering scope, schedule, budget, resourcing, dependencies and stage gates from contract signature through discovery, design, build, test, rollout, stabilisation and decommissioning of legacy systems.
Manage the implementation partner and the wider vendor estate: hold the implementation partner to contracted scope, deliverables, quality and commercials; run change control; and escalate commercial or performance issues through Procurement, Legal and the Executive Sponsor.
Own the project risk profile: identify, quantify and actively mitigate delivery risk — data migration, integration, scope creep, resource availability, adoption and legacy-platform continuity — and give governance bodies an honest view of confidence against milestones.
Steward the investment: manage the approved budget, track spend and forecast against variance, protect the contingency, and report cost position and benefit realisation to the Business Owner, SPOC, the other relevant governance bodies.
Lead business change and adoption: direct the change, communications, training and readiness effort across the Secretariat and Country Offices so that standardised finance processes are understood, accepted and used from go-live, and so that benefits are realised rather than assumed.
Safeguard quality and operational readiness: define acceptance criteria, own the testing and UAT regime, and confirm with Finance, GTDS and Cybersecurity that each release meets architecture, security, control and supportability standards before it is recommended for go-live.

Major Duties And Responsibilities

Project planning and delivery management

Develop, own and maintain the integrated Hazina delivery plan — scope, schedule, budget, resources, dependencies, assumptions and stage gates — covering discovery, design, build, configuration, data migration, integration, testing, training, rollout, stabilisation and legacy decommissioning.
Establish the programme team and operating rhythm: define roles, responsibilities and the delivery RACI across WWF and the implementation partner so that accountability for the plan, the budget and the go-live recommendation is unambiguous and the "who owns this" gaps do not arise.
Track progress against milestones and critical path, maintain the RAG position for the Systems Projects Oversight Committee reporting cycle, and proactively drive recovery actions as soon as slippage appears rather than reporting it after the fact.
Operate formal change control over scope, schedule and cost, ensuring every material change is assessed for benefit, risk and funding impact and approved at the right level of governance.

Stakeholder management and governance

Working with the Executive Sponsor and the Business Owner to ensure project governance is appropriately designed, implemented and fully functioning throughout the project lifecycle.
Prepare and present delivery reporting, decision papers and stage-gate submissions for the Systems Projects Oversight Committee, the Executive Team, and other relevant governance bodies for oversight of implementation.
Work with the Executive Sponsor, the Business Owner for Finance, and the GTDS leadership to align competing priorities, resolve escalations, and secure the decisions required to keep the project on track.
Build and hold the confidence of Country Directors, Finance Directors and Country Office focal points where adoption is influenced rather than instructed, and where local finance practice, capacity and connectivity vary widely.
Manage expectations candidly: set out trade-offs between scope, time, cost and quality with the evidence behind them, and hold a defensible position under challenge from senior stakeholders and committee members.

Budget and investment management

Manage the approved Hazina budget end to end: maintain the cost baseline, phase spend across FY27 to FY29, forecast to completion, explain variance and flag overrun risk before it compounds.
Identify and agree with GTDS Platforms and Finance the recurring costs after go-live — licences, environments, hosting, vendor support and integration services — so that they are budgeted and owned before the project closes.
Control the contingency deliberately, with a documented basis for every drawdown, and identify value-engineering and cost-avoidance opportunities with the implementation partner and Microsoft.
Own the benefits realisation plan: baseline the measures behind the assessed non-financial benefits, track them through and beyond go-live, and report realisation honestly to SPOC, the Executive Team and the other governance bodies.

Risk, issue and dependency management

Own the project risk and issue registers, with named owners, mitigations, triggers and target dates; actively manage the exposures that decide project outcomes — data migration and data quality, integration dependencies, scope creep, resource availability, partner performance, user adoption and business continuity.
Maintain the continuity position for the legacy finance systems through decommissioning, so that the organisation is never exposed to an unsupported platform and a partially delivered replacement at the same time, and agree with Finance, Internal Audit and GTDS how historical finance data is archived, retained and kept accessible for audit and reporting after each legacy system is switched off.
Escalate material architecture, data, cybersecurity, data protection, finance policy or compliance matters to the accountable authority — the GTDS Enterprise Solutions and Solution Architecture lead, the Director, Data, AI and Platforms, the Global CISO, the Director of Technology and Digital Services, or Finance leadership — rather than absorbing them within the project.
Ensure the project’s control environment, audit trail and documentation are sufficient for internal and external audit scrutiny at any point in delivery.

Resource, team and vendor management

Resource and mobilise the WWF side of the project: secure workstream leads, business process owners, subject matter experts and Country Office participation, and keep them available against competing operational demands.
Lead a multi-disciplinary, multi-location team without line authority — setting direction, resolving conflict, coaching, and sustaining pace and morale across a two-year delivery in multiple time zones, languages and operating contexts.
Manage the implementation partner day to day: agree and monitor the statement of work, deliverable acceptance, resource profile and rate card; challenge estimates and designs; and hold the partner to schedule, quality and knowledge-transfer commitments.
Work with Procurement and Legal on contract variations, service credits and commercial negotiation, and provide the evidence base for any escalation with the vendor.

Solution quality, data and operational readiness

Work within GTDS technical design authority: solution architecture, integration design and GTDS technology standards are set and approved by the GTDS Enterprise Solutions and Solution Architecture lead. The Senior Project Manager plans and runs delivery against them and escalates any conflict between schedule, cost and standards.
Drive the design and configuration agenda towards a standardised global core in line with the design principles: challenge customisation requests, protect the out-of-the-box position that the business case rests on, and ensure exceptions are justified, costed and approved.
Own the data migration plan with Finance and the Data, AI and Platforms team — scope, cleansing, mapping, reconciliation, dress rehearsals and sign-off criteria — and treat data readiness as a gating condition for go-live, not a parallel activity.
Ensure master data definitions, record identifiers and the system of record for each shared data area — including grants and awards, projects, offices and implementing entities, and budgets and expenditures — are agreed with GTDS data architecture and the Finance data owners, so that Hazina stays consistent with connected systems such as PI360, the grants management system.
Plan the transition of finance

Together, we are building a high-performance enterprise data infrastructure, developing outcome-oriented data products and enabling GIC’s transformation into a data-driven organisation.

As a risk-focused business analyst, you will partner with GIC’s top-of-the-house investment and risk professionals, shaping transformational capabilities that power critical investment data and analytics. You will lead strategic outcomes for GIC’s top-of-the-house investment and risk professionals, shaping transformational capabilities that power critical investment data and analytics. This role supports GIC’s vision of being a data- and technology-driven global long-term investment firm.

Join us if you are passionate about data and technology, and are motivated to lead the development of GIC’s enterprise data foundation, infrastructure and analytics capabilities.

4-8 years of relevant data and technology experience, preferably in financial services, risk or asset management, including collaborating with cross-functional business analysis, data and engineering teams to deliver impactful outcomes.

Developing structured plans for the execution of data and technology solutions to uplift processes in relation to business analytics.

Strong business leadership, with the ability to engage stakeholders across functions and seniority levels, and to collaborate with and influence cross-department business and technology partners in the development and execution of data and technology strategies.

Neuberger Wealth is seeking a highly motivated and results-driven individual to lead initiatives focused on process improvement and operational excellence. This individual will play a critical role in enhancing the efficiency, scalability, and effectiveness of the Neuberger Wealth business by evaluating current processes, identifying opportunities for improvement, and driving implementation efforts. The role requires a blend of strategic thinking, operational expertise, and change management capabilities.

As a member of the Wealth Platforms & Experience organization, the role of the Business Analyst will be responsible for the ownership and execution of several strategic programs and analyses related to Private Wealth’s Client Service Journey.

The candidate will be a detail oriented strategic thinker with a passion for solving complex problems, dealing with ambiguity, organizational design, and who possesses an unrelenting customer obsession and a strong desire to make their mark on the organization.

Primary Responsibilities:

Journey Definition

Own and enhance all aspects of the Client Service journey across the Wealth business (transacting, trading, maintenance, inquiry, self-service)
Create and maintain journey maps, process flows, SOPs, and playbooks and training materials across the end-to-end client onboarding journey
Identify friction points and recommend enhancements that reduce handoffs, processing times, and error rates
Analyze current operating model, inclusive of roles and responsibilities across all areas supporting the Client Service journey. Recommend and implement changes focused on efficiency and enhanced client outcomes
Establish and track SLAs and KPIs

Technology Enablement

Drive all aspects of technology enablement in the Client Service space inclusive of requirements creation, user testing, release coordination, and post-launch adoption and performance
Partner with Enterprise Data Governance to define and maintain client and account data dictionaries and validation rules. Ensure consistency across the ecosystem and all client and advisor touchpoints
Inventory and rationalize Client Service forms and documentation requirements with the goal of simplification of workflows
Maintain an inventory and prioritization of known tech debt / enhancements

Experience & Skills Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Finance, Operations Management, Engineering, or a related field
5+ years of experience in Wealth Management / Private Banking. Direct experience with client service, product ownership, or business analysis a plus
Strong knowledge of process mapping, workflow analysis, and operational efficiency tools
Proficiency in automation technologies and familiarity with digital transformation initiatives
Experience in change management principles and techniques
Candidate must be a self-starter with the ability to operate independently and make decisions
Ability to build relationships and partner across a complex organization
Ability to multi-task and manage multiple simultaneous projects
Ability to influence seniors and stakeholders outside of your span of control
Excellent time management, follow-through, and project delivery skills
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, able to simplify complexity
Exceptional analytical skills
Strategic thinker
Strong attention to detail
Highly organized
Owner of outcomes
Team player

Applicants must be authorized and have the right to work in the country where the role is located without the need for current or future sponsorship.

The salary range for this role is $90,000-$120,000. This is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. About Us

Since 1989, SHI International Corp. has helped organizations change the world through technology. We’ve grown every year since, and today we’re proud to be a $16 billion global provider of IT solutions and services.

Over 17,000 Organizations Worldwide Rely On SHI’s Concierge Approach To Help Them Solve What’s Next. But The Heartbeat Of SHI Is Our Employees – All 7,000 Of Them. If You Join Our Team, You’ll Enjoy

Our commitment to diversity, as the largest minority- and woman-owned enterprise in the U.S.
Continuous professional growth and leadership opportunities.
Health, wellness, and financial benefits to offer peace of mind to you and your family.
World-class facilities and the technology you need to thrive – in our offices or yours.

Job Summary

The Data Analyst collaborates with SHI management to support data-driven requests and initiatives, conducting data collection, analysis, and performance tracking across various segments. This role involves generating and merging reports from multiple databases, writing PowerBI reports, and performing ad-hoc analysis to identify opportunities and develop scenarios. The Data Analyst will assist with business cases, deliver monthly and quarterly reporting on financial and operational KPIs, and work closely with stakeholders to enhance data for analysis and performance management.

Role Description

Collaborate with SHI management to support numerous requests and project initiatives including from other SHI departments based on data.
Data collection & analysis of activity including forecasts across various segments and milestones.
Track & detail activity and performance against goals, forecasts and Plan.
Account Mapping by locating the appropriate salesperson for assigned list of leads.
Generate reports from multiple databases/data sets merging into spreadsheets and/or database.
Write reports in PowerBI for reporting and performance management.
Analyze, interpret, format, and summarize data for management review.
Work with stakeholders to obtain, validate, and enhance data utilized for analysis and performance tracking.
Perform ad-hoc analysis that aids in identifying opportunities, creating assumptions, and developing scenarios.
Assist with business cases defined with clear scope, intended outcomes, quantifiable benefits, and expenses.
Monthly and quarterly reporting focused on the entire portfolio of initiatives. This will include:
Financial performance: measure expense and savings on a profit and loss statement (P&L), cash flow impact, working capital impact, or productivity benefit.

Operational KPIs: tracking hours saved, utilization, # of instances, etc., depending on the project.

Commentary: work with initiative owners to identify drivers for the month, quarter, and future outcomes.

Behaviors and Competencies

Analytical Thinking: Can apply critical thinking to analyze data, identify patterns, and make basic inferences.
Data Analysis: Can identify patterns and trends in data, propose hypotheses, and use statistical techniques to test them.
Data Literacy: Can identify relevant data sources, collect data, and use basic tools to interpret and report findings.
Critical Thinking: Can analyze and interpret data to inform decision-making, and propose solutions based on logical reasoning.
Attention to Detail: Can identify errors or inconsistencies in work and make necessary corrections.
Communication: Can effectively communicate complex ideas and information, and can adapt communication style to the audience.
Problem-Solving: Can identify problems, propose solutions, and take action to resolve them without explicit instructions.
Technical Expertise: Can apply technical knowledge and skills effectively in most situations, with occasional guidance.
Time Management: Can generally use time effectively and is working towards improving task prioritization and deadline management.
Continuous Improvement: Can identify moderate areas for improvement and implement moderate changes.

Skill Level Requirements

Database management and reporting skills - Intermediate
Strong organizational skills - Intermediate
Experience with customer relations and satisfaction - Intermediate
Ability to multitask and complete tasks with efficiency and accuracy - Intermediate
Ability to follow direction while working individually and in a team environment - Intermediate
Ability to accept, understand, and learn from management feedback - Intermediate
Ability to work effectively within all levels of an organization, both internally and externally - Intermediate
Strong negotiation skills with the ability to influence stakeholders - Intermediate

Other Requirements

Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience required.
2-4 years of experience in a data and analysis-related field.
Advanced knowledge of Microsoft Excel & Access for reporting and database management
Proficient with Microsoft Office applications
Working knowledge of finance concepts, principles, and practices preferred.
